title.narrative: Strengthening Secondary Healthcare Services in Al Managil, Al-Jazirah State

description.narrative: ltpgtRelief International and UK-MED are collaborating to address critical health and nutrition needs, as well as integrate protection and WASH activities in Al Jazirah, particularly in Al Managil locality, currently experiencing a cholera outbreak and IPC level 4 food insecurity. The project aims to serve 64,009 individuals (38,963 females, 25,046 males), focusing on stabilizing and restoring secondary healthcare services. ltbrgt ltbrgtKey interventions include strengthening secondary healthcare, with an emphasis on operationalizing the outpatient and obstetrics/gynecological departments of Al Managil Hospital. The project will provide emergency trauma response and outbreak management, including establishing a Cholera Treatment Centre (CTC), Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), EPI services, and will integrate WASH in health facilities, and care for Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) survivors. Additionally, the hospital’s WASH infrastructure will be rehabilitated, improving access to clean water and sanitation, with gender-segregated latrines and showers for patients, caregivers, and staff. Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures will be implemented, supported by comprehensive training, supplies, and the management of medical waste. To ensure sustainable energy, a solar power system will be installed to support critical hospital services. ltbrgt ltbrgtThe project’s nutrition component focuses on treating children under five with Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) through both outpatient and inpatient care. Pregnant and breastfeeding women will also receive targeted supplementary feeding support. RI will build local capacity by training health workers in Community-based Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM), case management, and Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF). WASH kits will be distributed to malnourished children and women to support essential hygiene practices. Ongoing monitoring visits by the State Ministry of Health (SMOH) and RI staff will ensure the quality of care and provide on-the-job training where needed. ltbrgt ltbrgtProtection services will be integrated to support vulnerable groups, especially women and girls. A safe space (GBV corner) will be established at the hospital, offering SGBV case management, clinical management of rape, and referral services for those at risk or survivors of GBV. MHPSS services will be extended to both women and men, addressing the broader psychosocial needs of the community. ltbrgt ltbrgtIn line with the “do no harm” principle, conflict sensitivity will be woven into all project activities. RI will conduct conflict analyses, engage with local communities, and ensure transparent beneficiary selection to promote peace and reduce tensions. Regular risk assessments, flexible programming, and feedback mechanisms will guide the project’s adaptation to the volatile environment while maintaining community trust. ltbrgt ltbrgtUK-MED will further support Al Managil Hospital by providing remote technical assistance through Multidisciplinary Teams (MDTs), delivering expertise in secondary care, and enhancing local capacity through remote training. Over a 10-month period, the project will focus on managing 170 trauma consultations, supplemented by ongoing technical support to strengthen clinical capacity and fill gaps in care delivery. ltbrgt ltbrgtTogether, RI and UK-MED’s comprehensive approach will significantly reduce morbidity and mortality in Al Jazirah, while addressing the underlying causes of food insecurity, disease outbreaks, and vulnerabilities faced by the community.ltbrgtlt/pgt
